Definition: of Hebrew origin (H8256) in imitation of G4809; a sycamore-fig tree:--sycamine tree.
BiblicalUsage: The sycamine tree is the one faith can move. If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea, and it should obey you. A rooted tree, planted in the sea, by a word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tree is the measure of mustard-seed faith: it obeys, root and all, when the word is spoken.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
